Alten Merihall has taken much of the bay's outside trade since Lilmoth fell.
Lilmoth has no single ruler; a council of powerful merchants governs it and pays guards to patrol the streets.
On the bigger docks of the coast a ship's crew is often bought with somebody's months of owing, and the harbour calls it hiring.
In Lilmoth people take their quarrels to their elders, retired Shadowscales among them, not to a court.
Once, foreigners without a licence were kept to Lilmoth's docks and barred from the city.
West of Lilmoth the Ixtaxh Xanmeer lies silted and flooded again; only its topmost chamber stands above the mud.
About ten miles from Lilmoth stands a wall of mangroves so thick it is nearly impassable; the old story says the roots were giant spiders once.
In the lowlands east of Lilmoth stands the Xinchei-Konu Monument, an old stone calendar said to change the weather, with a keeper of its own.
Lilmoth is built over shallow water, so large ships cannot dock there; they anchor out and lighter boats bring the goods in.
A debt here is paid in work: an arbitrator turns the loss into months of labour, counted in nushmeekos, and when the months are worked it is over.
An owing can be sold on: a holder owed months can sell them to someone who needs hands, and the worker goes with them.
Lilmoth was destroyed long ago and built again smaller and lower, a stilt town, and nobody rebuilds the drowned old quarter.
Hereguard Plantation grows rice, and Lilmoth buys it.
Sea-drakes, crocodile-like beasts with paddle legs, live in the deep water off Lilmoth.
Lilmoth's Hist is tended in the open, behind a wall, and the tree-minder's post rotates so no one person ever listens to it alone.
An Argonian kept long from their own Hist fades: colour thins and markings go soft, and they come back when the person goes home.
